                                    On October 17, 1975 at 10 : 20 P.M . , Mr. c. Horne of 1
                                    Beaverbank Villa, Beaverbank, Nova Scotia, reported
                                    ad unidentified flying object to the Bedford R. C. M.
                                    Police Detachment . He observed the object in the
                                    Be~verbank area tot approximately one and one-half
                                    minutes. He described it as being a single light,
                                    approximately five · t housand feet high and ~t moved
                                    quickly from one point to another. The last part of
                                    the observation, it appeared to have a white tail.
                                    It was last seen heading in t he direction of the
                                    Hali~ax International Airport.
                        I       •


                                    Patrol was made to the area on this clear cool evening,
                                    but nothing was observed. Mr . HORNE was the onl_y
                                    person that called our Office about the object and
                                    it was felt that he was since.re a.nd hon~at in making
                                    the report altho~gh ' there is no explanation · at this
                                    point as to what he 'actuall y saw.

           4 JAN 76     (GOLDEN DETACHMENT CASE)       UNORGANIZED                                           .,,
                   al' James          of General Delive                                           B.C.
    l.           On the 5th -of Janu~ry, 1976 at 6:00P .M. , Mr. Mel HBINS of
    Box 23, Harrogate, B.Cryhoned- t:he Detachment to report an Unidfntified
    Flying Object.' The complainant claimed that he was driving his vehicle
    south on Highway #95 two to two and one half miles south of Parson, B.C.
    at approximately 22:15 Mountain Standard Time on the 4th of January, 1976
    when he observed several vehicl~s stopped along the• road and people
    watc hing something . The complainant stopped his vehicle and got out.,
    He ~aw a large triangular object in the sky. At the time, it was anowint
    heayily, overcast and dark. _The object had a leading red flashing light.
    Each of th~ tra~ling ends oi · l$triangle had a flashing blue light or
    a flashing ifreen light. The object made no noise as it travelled
    northbound. The object was approximated at travel~ing the aa~- speed
    ss a helicopt~r. The U. F.O. was thought to be flying about 100 feet
    above tree level and following the hydro lines. The witness described
    the craft as looking like it had a row of windows spaced far apart
    with lights inside. The object was observed for a short time until it
    was l ost from sight in the snow storm .                                ~

    2.          Hr. HEINS was the second person to report the incident. A
    Mr. James HUNT had reported the same occurrence earlier in the afternoon
    on the 5th of. January, 1976 . Mr~ · HUNT phoned fr~m ReveJ.stoke, B.C. aa
    he was on ~is way to his home in KAM~OOPS, B,C.       ·   '
                       .                                                                  .              '
    J.          A check of the helicopt&~ companies in the Golden a~ea
    showed that ther~were no l helicopters flying on the night in question.
    The Ministry ~f Transport advised that there were no reported fixed
    wing aircraft in the area . .                 ;           ~  '.
    4. '        The complai'nants are unknown to the investigators and it
\   is impossible to make a conclusion.
    5.          Parson is located 26 miles South of Go~den, B.C . in the
    Columbia River Valley.
